### Planner Response

Root cause found in your logs was **not only blur math** — it was **slider-drag save thrash**.

Your trace clearly showed repeated calls like:
- [saveColorPresets(...)](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt:92:4-102:5) from slider drag stack
- skipped frames + long frame times
- huge Compose methods ([AppLayoutPreview](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/ColorPickerDialog.kt:1055:0-2001:1), [ColorsSection](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/SettingsScreen.kt:1338:0-2460:1)) already under pressure

That makes blur feel “same/jumpy” even when mapping is corrected, because UI feedback is stuttering.

## Fix I applied

I removed per-frame preset persistence during photo edit slider drags in the **edit dialog** path:

- `onPhotoBlurChange`
- `onPhotoOffsetXChange`
- `onPhotoOffsetYChange`
- `onPhotoScaleChange`
- `onPhotoRotationChange`

Now these update only local edit state while dragging, and commit once on **Select/Test** via existing `onPhotoSelected`.

### Code refs
- `@app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/SettingsScreen.kt#3231-3257`

This specifically removes the per-tick `onEditCustomColor(...)` cascade that was hitting [loadColorPresets()/saveColorPresets()](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt:104:4-119:5) repeatedly through [MainActivity](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt:52:0-4400:1) handlers.

## Validation

- Build: `./gradlew.bat :app:compileDebugKotlin` ✅

- `@CHANGELOG.md#13-47`
- `@CHAT_HISTORY.md#3-31`

### Planner Response

Implemented a direct fix for the behavior you described.

I followed your saved preferences from memory:  
- **Global development/documentation rules**, and  
- **Build/test reporting format** (what done + root cause + exact next tests).

## 1) What I changed

I removed the hard 8% dead zone from the shared blur mapping and switched to a **continuous smooth ramp** so blur starts from the first slider movement.

- Updated: `@app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt#6-16`
  - Removed `PHOTO_BLUR_DEAD_ZONE = 0.08f`
  - Replaced thresholded cubic mapping with:
    - `smoothRamp = t * t * (3 - 2 * t)`
    - `radius = smoothRamp * 5f`

Also updated required docs:
- `@CHANGELOG.md#13-44`
- `@CHAT_HISTORY.md#3-35`

Build check:
- `:app:compileDebugKotlin` ✅ **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**

---

## 2) Main problem / root cause

Your report was accurate: the mapping had a hard cutoff at 8%.  
That meant:

- `0%..7.99%` => always `0dp` blur (no visible change),
- then crossing 8% felt like a sudden jump.

So the issue was not slider UI itself; it was the mapping function’s dead-zone logic.

---

## 3) Exactly what to test next

### 1) What was done

I changed the shared blur mapping to a **strict linear ramp** so each 1% slider movement increases blur proportionally (no easing curve).

- Updated: `@app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/BlurMapping.kt#8-14`
  - From eased curve: `t * t * (3 - 2 * t)`
  - To linear: `t * PHOTO_BLUR_MAX_RADIUS_DP`
- Kept max blur cap unchanged (`5dp`).
- Build validation:
  - `./gradlew.bat :app:compileDebugKotlin` ✅ **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**
- Docs updated:
  - `@CHANGELOG.md#13-46`
  - `@CHAT_HISTORY.md#3-35`

### 2) Main problem / root cause

Even after removing the old 8% dead zone, the remaining **smoothstep non-linear mapping** still made low-end blur feel abrupt once it became visible.  
You asked for strictly incremental behavior from 1% to 100%, so the non-linear curve had to be removed in favor of linear mapping.

5. Press **Select/Test**, reopen the same preset, and confirm the behavior persists.

### 2) Main problem / root cause

The abrupt feel was no longer mainly from blur mapping math.  
Your logs showed the edit/preview path was flooding `Log.d(...)` on nearly every slider tick/recomposition, including repeated “Opening EDIT ColorPickerDialog…” and preview logs. That extra main-thread overhead caused jank/stalls, making blur changes look sudden instead of smooth.

---

### 3) Exactly what you should test next

1. Open **Settings -> Colors -> File List Background** photo editor.
2. Drag blur slowly from `0%` upward (very small moves).
3. Confirm preview updates continuously (no sudden stepping/jumpiness).
4. Repeat in **File List Item** editor to compare behavior.
5. Optional: keep Logcat open and verify those repeated `ColorPreview` / `UnifiedBgEditor` / [ColorPresetRow](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/SettingsScreen.kt:2510:0-3278:1) spam lines are gone during drag.

I followed your global rules + your build/test reporting preference (what done, root cause, exact next tests).

### Planner Response

I followed the **“build/test report format” memory** (the one requiring: what was done, root cause, and exactly what to test next).

## 1) What I changed

I applied a root-cause performance fix so blur preview stays smooth during drag:

- **Stopped per-tick preset disk writes in blur callbacks** (kept only in-memory selected preset sync while dragging):  
  @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt#3328-3335  
  @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt#3419-3426  
  @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt#3510-3517  
  @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt#3601-3608  
  @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt#3689-3696

- **Removed remaining hot-path PhotoControls logs** in render/chip click paths:  
  @app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/PhotoControlsPanel.kt#140-167

- **Updated documentation**:
  - @CHANGELOG.md#13-51
  - @CHAT_HISTORY.md#3-41

- **Compile check passed**:
  - `.\gradlew.bat :app:compileDebugKotlin` ✅ BUILD SUCCESSFUL

---

## 2) Main problem / root cause

Blur mapping itself was already improved, but preview still felt abrupt because the UI thread was getting hammered during slider drag:

- `on*PhotoBlurChange` in [MainActivity](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt:52:0-4355:1) still performed preset persistence work on every slider tick ([loadColorPresets](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt:104:4-119:5)/[saveColorPresets](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/MainActivity.kt:92:4-102:5) path).
- Remaining high-frequency `Log.d` calls in [PhotoControlsPanel](file:///c:/Users/javie/AndroidStudioProjects/TeXter2025/app/src/main/java/com/j4/texter2025/ui/components/PhotoControlsPanel.kt:30:0-206:1) added extra overhead.

That combo caused frame drops, making blur appear to “jump” instead of update continuously.

---

## 3) Exactly what you should test next

1. Open **Settings → Colors → File List Background → photo editor**.  
2. Drag **Blur** slowly from `0%` upward continuously.  
3. Confirm preview changes are smooth (no abrupt stepping/stutter).  
4. Repeat in **File List Item** photo editor.  
5. Tap **Select/Test**, close/reopen editor, and confirm values still apply correctly.
